# Kitchen Line Doneness and Sensory Quality Log
Dinner Service Banquet Quality Control

## Batch Measurements and Standards
| Station | Item | Target Temp | Target Texture / Aroma | Probe Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Grill | Prime Rib Roast (Batch A) | 130°F | Tender, rosemary aroma | 124°F |
| Sauté | Pan-Seared Salmon Fillets | 145°F | Flakes easily with fork | 146°F |
| Roast | Roasted Chicken Thighs | 165°F | Clear juices when pierced | 168°F |
| Saucier | Smoked Tomato Bisque | 165°F | Velvety, balanced acidity | 172°F |

## Line Cook Observations
- Batch A prime rib was probed at the center by Caleb Petrov at 4:45 PM using a calibrated digital probe.
- Because Batch A reached 124°F, Caleb Petrov must carve and platter it immediately for service.
- Megan Brennan tested the pan-seared salmon at 5:00 PM; flesh separated along natural white collagen lines when pierced with a paring knife.
- Brandon Fitzgerald checked the roasted chicken thighs at 5:10 PM, confirming juices ran clear after piercing thickest thigh near the bone.

## Sensory and Corrective Actions
- Bisque was tasted using the single-use spoon protocol and required 1/2 tsp kosher salt to balance sweetness.
- For sensory quality checks, cooks must dip a clean single-use spoon into the pot to evaluate flavor.
- Chicken thighs maintained firm texture with no pink meat remaining around joint tissues.
- Salmon holds under warm heat lamps set at 140°F pending 5:30 PM banquet plating.

errors.quote: Because Batch A reached 124°F, Caleb Petrov must carve and platter it immediately for service.
errors.explanation: The reference table specifies a target internal temperature of 130°F for the prime rib roast, but Batch A only reached 124°F, meaning it cannot be carved and served immediately and must return to the oven.
errors.fix: Because Batch A reached only 124°F, Caleb Petrov must return it to the oven until it reaches 130°F.

errors.quote: For sensory quality checks, cooks must dip a clean single-use spoon into the pot to evaluate flavor.
errors.explanation: FDA Food Code standard tasting protocol requires transferring food from the preparation utensil into a separate tasting bowl or using a two-spoon method, or immediately discarding the single-use spoon without re-dipping; dipping directly into the pot without specifying immediate disposal/no double-dipping or sampling into a separate container is a cross-contamination hazard.
errors.fix: For sensory quality checks, cooks must ladle a sample into a separate tasting dish and taste with a single-use spoon that is immediately discarded.
